input.quote: 22.1 Governing Law. The validity, construction and interpretation of this Agreement and the rights and duties of the parties hereto shall be governed by the internal laws of the State of Wisconsin, excluding its principles of conflict of laws.
input.rationale: Section 22.1 selects Wisconsin internal law and Section 22.2 fixes exclusive venue in Milwaukee County and the Eastern District of Wisconsin — M&I's home forum and outside the accepted list (New York, Delaware, California, England and Wales), so the clause fails the fallback on its governing law and forum. There is no arbitration agreement (Article 15 is a non-binding executive escalation; the references to an "arbitrator" in 22.10 and 22.11 are residual boilerplate only), so this is a deviation rather than walk-away. We therefore move only the jurisdiction words and the forum to the preferred position: New York internal law and exclusive venue in the state and federal courts in New York County. The remaining second sentence of 22.2 is a mutual post-judgment enforcement consent for courts where a judgment debtor's assets sit, not a merits-forum carve-out, so exclusivity for litigation to enforce the Agreement is preserved and Customer's enforcement flexibility is not weakened.

proposal.summary: Move governing law to New York and venue to the state and federal courts in New York County.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have moved the governing law from Wisconsin to New York and the exclusive venue to the state and federal courts in New York County, consistent with our playbook's accepted jurisdictions; Delaware, California or England and Wales (with London courts) would also work as a fallback. The rest of Sections 22.1 and 22.2, including the post-judgment enforcement consent, is unchanged.

ops.newText: the internal laws of the State of New York

ops.oldText: the courts of Milwaukee County, Wisconsin and the Federal District Court for the Eastern District of Wisconsin
ops.newText: the state and federal courts located in New York County, New York
